seoTitle: SSH Key Pair Generator (Ed25519, ECDSA, RSA) in Your Browser
metaDescription: Generate an OpenSSH key pair in the browser: public key line for authorized_keys and an OpenSSH private key. Created with WebCrypto, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Create an SSH key for servers, Git hosting or CI without installing anything.
why:
Pick Ed25519, ECDSA (P-256 or P-384) or RSA (3072 or 4096 bits) and an optional comment. WebCrypto generates the key, and the page writes the public key line, the SHA-256 fingerprint and the private key in the OpenSSH format. All four key types were verified with ssh-keygen -y and ssh-keygen -l, which derived the same public keys and fingerprints.

The private key is not passphrase-protected; add one with ssh-keygen -p. A key made in a web page is only as trustworthy as the page and device, so for high-value keys generate them on the machine that will keep them.

The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
howTo: Choose the key type and comment.
Copy the public key line and the private key.
Save the private key with permissions 600 and add the public key to authorized_keys.

faq.a: Ed25519 is small, fast and widely supported; use RSA 3072+ only for old systems.

faq.q: Is it safe to generate keys in a browser?
faq.a: The key is made locally with the browser's crypto, but the safest place for important keys is the device that will use them.

faq.q: Can I add a passphrase here?

faq.a: The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
